extracted.intended_audience: natural philosophers and botanists (readers of the Royal Society / Philosophical Transactions)
extracted.subtask_description: Specification for composing a phytological (botanical) natural history and the anatomy section on roots: what surveys, analyses, figures, and topics it should contain. Focused guidance for organizing observational, anatomical, and compositional study of plants.

rubrics_metrics.name: Survey of external characteristics of plants
rubrics_metrics.description: A particular and comparative survey of what relates to the more external consideration about vegetables; as of their figures, proportions, seasons, places, motions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Collect comparative, detailed observations of external morphology and ecology (shape, proportions), phenology (seasons), geographic/locality (places), and movements; present comparisons across specimens/species.

rubrics_metrics.name: Anatomical survey of organical parts
rubrics_metrics.description: A like survey of the organical parts by anatomy, and how that is 'to be prosecuted, both without and with a microscope; from thence we may come to know, what the communities of vegetables are as belonging to all; what their distinctions to such a kind; their properties to such a species; and their particularities to such particular ones.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Perform anatomical study at macroscopic and microscopic scales; use dissections and microscopy to identify shared structures, genus/species-level distinctions, typical properties, and individual peculiarities.

rubrics_metrics.name: Survey of internal contents (saps, oils, gums, etc.)
rubrics_metrics.description: A like survey of the contents of vegetables; of their several kinds, as spirits, airs and vapors, clear saps, milks, oils, gums, sugars, salts, &c. examined in all manner of ways.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Analyze and document the chemical/physical contents of plant tissues (liquids, resins, volatiles, sugars, salts); use multiple methods of examination and report differences across taxa and organs.

rubrics_metrics.name: Survey of principles of organical parts (functional principles)
rubrics_metrics.description: A like survey of the principles as well as the contents of the organical parts. Whence will be attainable a further knowledge of the modes of vegetation, and of the sensible natures of vegetables, as also of their more recluse faculties and powers.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Investigate underlying principles (functional/physiological) of organs together with contents to deduce modes of growth/vegetation, observable properties, and less obvious faculties or powers of plants.

rubrics_metrics.name: Survey of environmental and associated bodies
rubrics_metrics.description: A like survey of those bodies, either from which these principles are derived, or wherewith they have any communion; which are earth, and all solid receptacles; water, and all liquid receptacles; air and sun.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Study and report how external media and substrates (soil/solids, water/liquids, air, and sunlight) interact with plant principles; include environmental/contextual data as part of the history.

rubrics_metrics.name: Overarching explanatory aim (assembly into vegetable body)
rubrics_metrics.description: In what manner these principles are so adapted as to become capable of being assembled together in such a number, connection, proportion and union, as to make a vegetable body?
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Treat the central question as the work's organizing aim: synthesize observations to explain how components/principles combine to produce a living plant body (integration of data across surveys).

rubrics_metrics.name: Include figures and explication for microscopical observations
rubrics_metrics.description: The Figures of some of Mr. Leewenhoek's Microscopical Observations, formerly published ... with their Explication.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provide detailed illustrative figures of microscopic observations accompanied by explicit labels and explanations of parts, motions, and interpretations (e.g., as done for the bee stings and head appendages).

rubrics_metrics.name: Root anatomy — the skin (epidermis)
rubrics_metrics.description: The skin, its external accidents and original, its compounding parts, the one parenchymous, consisting of bubbles, the other ligneous, consisting of tubulary vessels.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Describe the root epidermis: origin, external features, and internal composition distinguishing parenchymous (bubbly) tissue from ligneous (tubular vessel) components.

rubrics_metrics.name: Root anatomy — the bark (periderm/cortex)
rubrics_metrics.description: The bark; its original and external accidents, its compounding parts, likewise parenchymous, and ligneous; which latter consists of succiferous vessels, conjoined in threads, but no where inosculated, nor ramified, but distinct as the fibres of a nerve, which vessels are of various kinds, denominated from their contents, as lymphaeducts, lacteals, &c.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Document bark origin, external characters, composition (parenchymous and ligneous), and the arrangement/types of sap-conducting vessels (succiferous vessels), noting whether they ramify or remain distinct.

rubrics_metrics.name: Root anatomy — inner portion within the bark
rubrics_metrics.description: That portion of the root within the bark, of the like composition with the former, and its ligneous part, compounded of succiferous and air-vessels.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examine and report the inner root tissues (within the bark), focusing on composition similar to outer parts and the presence/structure of succiferous and air-vessels; compare to animal tissues where useful.

rubrics_metrics.name: Root anatomy — the pith
rubrics_metrics.description: The pith, not common to all roots; its origin, parenchymous nature, and texture, like to a rete mirabile, of an infinite number of small fibres admirably complicated together; its contents being sometimes a limpid liquor, sometimes a vaporous air.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Describe the presence/absence of pith, its origin and parenchymous microstructure (rete-like fibre network), and variability of contents (liquid or gaseous).
